html:
The Eleutheran Adventurers were Puritans from Bermuda who settled the Bahamas in 1648, seeking freedom of worship. They named their island Eleuthera, from the Greek word for freedom.

Led by William Sayle, they were wrecked on a reef as they arrived and lived for a time in a cave, where they held services. They had little to live on and survived by wrecking, salvaging ships lost on the reefs, and with help from New England.

Their colony was small and poor, but it began English settlement of the islands that had been empty since the loss of the Lucayans. Others soon followed to New Providence, where Nassau grew up, in the shadow of the pirates.
